title: centralize-tool-versions-and-split-ci-caches-to-reduce-flakiness
author: Marco Chen
release_notes: Improve CI reliability and developer onboarding: centralized toolchain versions, deterministic cache keying (per-language/arch), added lightweight ci-health smoke job, removed legacy CI scripts, updated CONTRIBUTING.md.
description:
Motivation: our CI has sporadic cache collisions and subtle local vs CI tool mismatches (go/node/python/terraform versions spread across scripts and workflow files). That has led to intermittent flakes and onboarding friction. This PR centralizes tool versions, separates caches to avoid cross-language invalidation, and adds a fast ci-health smoke job to surface regressions quickly.

What I changed (high-level):
- Add tooling/versions.toml as the single source of truth for pinned tool versions (go, node, python, tf, gh, docker). Workflows and helper scripts read from this file.
- Refactor .github/workflows/* to use a shared action (actions/ci-tooling-lookup) for deterministic setup and to compute cache keys. Cache keys are now per-language + os + arch + tool-version (reduces accidental cache reuse).
- Introduce .github/workflows/ci-health.yml: runs a small matrix (linux|mac runner emulation via container, latest node/go) that executes a curated smoke set (fast unit-critical tests + bootstrap). This job is required-for-merge and is intentionally lightweight (~2m).
- Split cache scopes: node-modules cache, go-build cache, pip-cache, terraform-plugin-cache; each keyed independently.
- Pin frequently-changing composite actions to SHAs for reproducible CI. Added a short script to refresh SHAs and a small doc section.
- Dependabot: adjust .github/dependabot.yml to ignore transitive updates for deep nested build-tool deps to avoid noisy PR churn.
- Remove scripts/ci_legacy.sh (dead, replaced by scripts/ci_bootstrap.sh) and clean up Makefile targets.
- Update CONTRIBUTING.md with explicit local bootstrap steps that use tooling/versions.toml and how to run ci-health locally.

Checklist (done):
